proposition: Specific peer boundaries and later school membership can coexist because the two refer to different events, relations and time frames.
supporting_evidence: Complete-sample boundary and belonging items; linked-case contrasts
counterevidence_or_limit: The strict high-high configuration contains fewer than three records and is suppressed; retrospective scales compress timing
rival_explanation: Measurement compression and ordinary newcomer transition
current_study_support: Supports coexistence descriptively, not a transition mechanism
future_test: Repeated measures of boundary events and multidimensional belonging across the first school year

proposition: A structured task can become both a hidden-rule learning site and a peer-entry opportunity when participation is made comprehensible and an invitation is available.
supporting_evidence: Group-project difficulty was common; linked event chains join task, explanation and invitation
counterevidence_or_limit: The clearest complete event chain is case-specific and cannot establish direction
rival_explanation: Teacher assignment, group composition or pre-existing friendliness
evidence_scope: Complete-sample task item plus linked cases
future_test: Observe task grouping, explanations and subsequent interactions prospectively

proposition: Support may be more usable when source, timing, visibility and need fit each other; receiving support alone may be insufficient.
supporting_evidence: Support effectiveness categories and contrasting linked accounts of peer, teacher and family help
counterevidence_or_limit: Need severity and self-selection can reverse simple comparisons
rival_explanation: More resourced students may both obtain support and report better outcomes
current_study_support: Supports three distinct support states; configuration is exploratory
future_test: Measure need before support, exposure, timing, uptake and outcome separately

proposition: Same-background ties can provide early safety and rule translation while, in some settings, reducing incentives to expand local ties.
supporting_evidence: One linked account explicitly described both safety and reduced local-contact motivation; survey shows same-background help and old-network support
counterevidence_or_limit: Only one explicit trade-off account; other cases retained prior ties without the same consequence
evidence_scope: One linked case contextualised by survey distributions
current_study_support: Not sufficient for a body-report conclusion
future_test: Longitudinal network maps and interviews about tie choice

proposition: Rule understanding, task burden and ability judgments are non-equivalent and can coexist in the same retrospective configuration.
supporting_evidence: Five reportable high-difficulty/high-rule-understanding configurations; linked accounts distinguish rules, language and workload
counterevidence_or_limit: Cross-sectional retrospective scores cannot establish change or order
rival_explanation: Prior attainment, selective persistence or item interpretation
current_study_support: Supports coexistence and non-equivalence, not temporal change
future_test: Repeated measures of clarity, workload, performance and self-concept

proposition: Peer invitations can matter because they alter immediate access, while institutional grouping rules determine whether such invitations are necessary or possible.
supporting_evidence: Linked contrasts between free grouping, teacher-arranged proximity and peer initiation
counterevidence_or_limit: Invitation effects are participant attributions and small-case evidence
rival_explanation: Friendly disposition, seat location or prior contact
future_test: Compare randomly varying or naturally changing grouping policies with observed tie formation

proposition: Survey responses are more consistent with platform coexistence and functional allocation than simple replacement; adoption alone does not establish a local peer network.
supporting_evidence: WeChat continuity, WhatsApp/Instagram adoption, functional items and network-pattern contrasts
counterevidence_or_limit: Interview event evidence for digital mechanisms is sparse and survey functions are self-reported
rival_explanation: School requirements, platform popularity and relationship continuity
evidence_scope: Complete questionnaire with limited linked elaboration
current_study_support: Supports a media-repertoire description; does not verify network effects
future_test: Digital diary plus ego-network and interaction-sequence data

proposition: Current evidence establishes only a few mediation events and cannot establish repeated behaviour, recognition or a stable role identity.
supporting_evidence: Survey mediation items contrast with very few concrete linked actions and a weak prior brokerage-belonging association
counterevidence_or_limit: Interviews may not have elicited all mediation episodes
evidence_scope: Complete questionnaire and three linked cases
current_study_support: Supports a stricter evidentiary distinction, not a claim that mediation is inherently episodic
future_test: Event sampling of translation acts, network position and recognition by others

proposition: Leaving a Hong Kong school pathway can coexist with retained relationships or learning practices, challenging a single linear adaptation endpoint.
supporting_evidence: Linked trajectory evidence includes selective retention after pathway change
counterevidence_or_limit: One restricted case carries the clearest exit-and-retention sequence
rival_explanation: Assessment pressure, family planning and mobility constraints
evidence_scope: One focal trajectory plus cross-case comparison
future_test: Follow movers across pathway decisions and measure retained practices and ties

proposition: A fixed integration type is sufficient to explain students' adaptation trajectories.
supporting_evidence: Within-case variation across peer, academic, platform and temporal domains
counterevidence_or_limit: Only three linked cases; contradiction is analytic rather than population-wide
rival_explanation: A more granular typology might still describe limited domains
evidence_scope: Three linked cases and complete-sample domain measures
current_study_support: Current evidence argues against this strong proposition
future_test: Test domain-specific and time-varying profiles prospectively

proposition: High scores on mediation items identify a stable cultural-broker role.
supporting_evidence: Two self-report items alone do not show repeated acts, recognition or role identity
evidence_scope: Complete questionnaire with sparse linked event evidence
future_test: Combine observed acts, alters' reports and repeated network measures
